subject: Private hosting handoff scenarios — decision checkpoint
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting options and next steps

Hi Jordan / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a little more granularity on what a Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment would look like from an operational ownership perspective. Specifically they want: 

- A short list of which Redwood teams own which responsibilities during pilot and GA (on-call, network config, KMS/hsm integration, software updates).
- A rough FTE / contractor estimate for standing up an on-prem pilot and then supporting GA (first 6 months).
- Any gaps that would require changes to our network or SRE processes (e.g., egress rules, peering, audit log shipping) that could impact our timeline.

They also attached the security checklist (attached: acme_security_checklist.pdf) — they noted SOC2 scope and key management are blockers for them. Can you get back with a short decision recommendation (pilot vs managed private) and a proposed owner list by COB Friday?

Appreciate it —
Sanjay
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Analytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private hosting options and next steps — quick internal run-through

Team — forwarding Acme's note. They want a short, actionable recommendation and an owner list by EOD Friday (they mean this coming Friday; timeline is tight). High-level asks below, please reply with concrete items I can pass back. Keep answers brief — bullets are fine.

Ask list: 
- Which Redwood teams will own: on-call, network setup, KMS/HSM integration, control-plane updates, and audit log ingestion for the private deployment?
- Pilot staffing: minimum FTEs and whether contractors are needed (estimate 6-month support).
- Major blockers / gating items that could push timeline beyond 6 weeks for a pilot.

I propose we recommend a 6-week pilot (minimal features) unless someone objects. Marcus — can you sketch a minimal pilot architecture and a staffing ask? Priyom — highlight compliance blockers. Laura — product gating criteria (what to include in pilot vs GA). I'll stitch into a single response.

-Jordan

Attachment: acme_security_checklist.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private hosting options and next steps — infra notes

Quick infra notes / minimal pilot sketch (bullets):

- Pilot topology (minimal): 1 VPC peered to customer transit (static peering / VPN), dedicated serving cluster (2x A100-equivalent nodes) behind LB, isolated control-plane with read-only telemetry export to customer SIEM.
- Ownership (pilot):
  - Network setup + VPN/peering: Redwood Cloud Network (infra) — owner: Marcus Lin (onboarding week 1).
  - Serving runtime updates & rollouts: Redwood Runtime team — co-owner (will need a single eng lead on-call for the pilot).
  - Control-plane ops (config sync, secret sync): Product Ops + infra (shared responsibility).
  - KMS/HSM integration: Security & infra (requires Priyom + one infra engineer for integration work).
- Staffing estimate (pilot): minimum 0.6 FTE infra (contractor friendly), 0.4 FTE runtime engineer, 0.2 FTE product-ops, 0.2 FTE security/integration (total ~1.4 FTE for first 6 weeks). For GA, expect 2.5–3.5 FTE ongoing depending on support SLA.
- Blockers & gating items:
  - Customer requires air-gapped binary distribution => increases effort by 3–4 weeks and +1 FTE for packaging/testing.
  - KMS/HSM (if they require on-prem HSM): we need a product decision on whether we support customer-managed keys on private control-plane or recommend holding keys in customer KMS only.
  - Audit log export format & retention SLA — must align with customer SOC2 evidence requirements.

Attachment: infra_pilot_estimate.xlsx

Note: runtime changes for quantization/optimized kernels are minimal for pilot but if Acme requires long-context (>16k) we'll need additional perf work (adds ~2 weeks).
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — product gating & rollout

Short product perspective for the pilot: 

- Pilot goals (must-haves): authenticated inference API, model pinning, telemetry export to customer SIEM, and a simple rollback path.
- Nice-to-haves (GA): auto-scaling, multi-model routing, per-tenant cost telemetry.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot -> GA: 
  - Security: pass baseline items in attached Acme checklist (key items: key custody, audit logs, vulnerability scan results).
  - Reliability: 99.5% env uptime during pilot window and verified rollback within 5 minutes.
  - Ops: documented runbook for deploys & incident triage; at least one SRE runbook dry-run before customer demo.
- Control-plane decision: recommend managed control-plane (Redwood-hosted, customer VPN to access) for pilot to reduce ops burden and speed timeline. If customer insists on full customer-managed control plane we escalate to product execs — that will add ~6 weeks and additional headcount.

I'll own the product gating checklist and will work with Marcus to map infra acceptance criteria.

-Laura
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — compliance notes

Couple of compliance/secure-deployment notes: 

- SOC2 scoping: If Acme requires Redwood artifacts (build/release pipelines) included in their SOC2, we need legal + compliance to evaluate. That significantly expands documentation needs (~3–4 weeks of prep).
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed HSM requires a signed responsibility matrix & an integration checklist; technically doable but expect extra validation and on-site/remote attestation steps.
- Audit logs: Customer retention request (7 years) vs our default (90 days) — need contract clarity. 7 years means we either push long-term retention to customer's storage or add an archived export process (legal + billing implications).
- Evidence & timelines: for pilot, request that Acme accepts a scoped set of evidence (deployment diagrams, logs for 30 days, vuln scan) rather than full SOC2 artifacts. If they insist on full SOC2 evidence before pilot, pilot timeline will slip.

Blocking ask: Priyom needs explicit decision on managed control-plane vs customer-managed by EOD Monday to prepare integration checklist.

-Priyom
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acmeanalytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting options — recommendation and next steps

Sanjay — thanks for the checklist and patience. Internal summary / recommended path below (short):

Recommendation: Run a 6-week pilot using a managed Redwood control-plane with customer VPC peering (minimal features: API + model pinning + telemetry export). This minimizes up-front headcount and speeds the first demo while keeping KMS options flexible.

Owners (pilot):
- Infra & network lead (onboarding/setup): Marcus Lin (owner)
- Product gating & acceptance: Laura Bennett (owner)
- Security & compliance integration: Priyom Das (owner)
- Sales / customer comms: Jordan Blake (owner)

Staffing ask (pilot): ~1.4 FTE (mix of 2 infra/runtime engineers + part-time product-ops & security support). GA staffing TBD after pilot; expect 2.5–3.5 FTE if we commit to 24/7 on-call and faster SLAs.

Blockers that would change recommendation:
- If Acme requires customer-managed control-plane or air-gapped distribution we will need an additional 4–6 weeks and +1–2 FTE.
- If they require SOC2-level evidence as a precondition for pilot we must escalate to legal/compliance and timeline will shift.

Next steps (action items):
1) Marcus to share minimal infra runbook + estimated start date (due Tuesday EOD).
2) Priyom to produce integration checklist assuming managed control-plane (due Tuesday EOD).
3) Laura to produce acceptance criteria doc & runbook skeleton (due Wednesday).
4) Jordan to confirm with Acme that managed control-plane pilot is acceptable and to schedule a kickoff call (target: Wed morning).

If Acme confirms managed control-plane, we'll move forward on the 6-week pilot. If not, we'll provide a revised estimate for customer-managed control-plane.

-Jordan

cc: legal@redwood.ai (informal)
